title: Less Intuitive With Every Update
body:
I’ve been a paying subscriber for nearly two years, largely because I meticulously track my workouts and didn’t want to lose my training history.

I won’t be renewing.

What originally attracted me to Boostcamp was its clean, intuitive design. Over time, the app has become increasingly cluttered with programming I don’t use, and features that were once easy to access have been buried behind additional taps.

A perfect example is workout history. There used to be a simple calendar view that made it easy to see every day you trained and quickly review your consistency month by month. Now that view is tucked away, making something I used regularly harder to find for no apparent benefit.

The exercise library is also more limited than it should be, with many common variations missing. 

I’ve stayed this long because my workout history is valuable to me, but the user experience has steadily declined. Moving years of training data to a new platform will be a hassle, but at this point it’s worth it.

If you value simple design, intuitive navigation, and quick access to your workout history, there are much better and cheaper options out there.

title: The best workout app
body:
Let me start by saying I’ve tried many things. Notebooks, excel, other apps,  etc… for extended periods of time before finding Boostcamp. 

This is the only app I’ve stuck to and used consistently, 5 days a week for… most of 3 years, since Jan 2024. Ive used the paid version for nearly 1 yr.

The free version is more than good enough, but the paid version allows for more customization.

This app is great for a couple of reasons. First it promotes consistency, and second it promotes personal investment in working out.  

How: a routine paired with intuitive tracking of progress takes all the guess work out of the gym. This is coming from someone who works 12 hour days and rarely knows what day it even is. This app rules because I go into the gym and just click start on whatever day is next in my routine. Set it and forget it. 

As for personal investment in the grind, this app motivates you by allowing you to change up YOUR routine and record YOUR progress… it gives YOU ownership and makes it easy instead of the focus being a product or fitness influencer.. it makes it about you. Then on top of that the app rewards you, when you make a PR it tells you, when you finish a workout it tells you. When you are consistent it tells you. It leverages our human propensity for rewards. 

Lastly the team is great. I had an issue with access and they helped me get it sorted out within hours. They have amazing user support which is unheard for imo for applications.

title: Used to be good. Now it’s far from.
body:
This app used to be much better, and I’m not talking about UI choices. I’m seriously considering switching apps at this point, but I feel locked in because all my old workout history is stored here. The behavior has really gone downhill recently (vibe coded?), e.g.

The workout progress on the lock screen rarely shows up anymore. This used to be essential for me timing my rest.

Data does not sync between the web and mobile versions well, losing data. I’m completely fed up with this because I wasted near an hour today trying to edit a program, and then opening it in the app reverted everything I did.

The program creator is buggy because it combines sets of the same number of reps, so you cannot edit them on the web version; the editor shows different numbers than the viewer. It will also have the wrong number of sets listed at times, and it loses the sets and reps suggested for exercise alternatives.

Certain custom exercises do not show up in exercise search some days. I cannot notice a pattern in this.

Some exercises are duplicate if you create a custom exercise with the same name as one that is later officially added to the app.

There are way too many buttons to press to add a note to exercises during a workout. Why is it fewer buttons to swap exercises than it is to add a quick note to what I did?

Reordering exercises is a total pain. It is glitchy and will swap exercises I did not intend to. It requires a ton of scrolling just to find the right buttons. Similarly, adding an exercise has to be done at the end of a workout and then reordered to the middle, the pain of which I’ve just described.

Web and mobile program editing is different, and I have to switch between the two just to get the options I want. For example, I cannot delete exercises from existing programs on web, but I can on mobile. On the other hand, I cannot add an exercise alternative on mobile, but I can on web. Combine this with the glitches around sets and reps, as well as the data loss, and I’m about as upset as can be just trying to get a simple workout programmed.

title: Good App Bad Architecture
body:
I am a pro user who uses this app 4-5 times a week for around 10h a week. I love the app, it has great features and programs, and I’ve been using it for a few years. 

Over time, the latency in the app has gotten really bad. It’s often unresponsive and takes 10-20 seconds to do something simple, like trying to pick a different day in a program than the immediate next session (which comes up if I have to cut a week short, etc), or swapping an exercise, or loading analytics. This, I think, is an architecture problem. I have a new iPhone and don’t run anything else except sometimes a music app in combo with this one.

Hope you guys can fix this soon! Thanks for everything you do.

title: Used to be great and now ruined by greed
body:
I’ve been a long-time user of this app since day one. I still remember the original Reddit post from the developer—there was real excitement and a refreshing openness to community feedback. It felt great to see user-requested features being thoughtfully implemented.

Unfortunately, over time, that spirit has faded. With each update, more previously free features are being moved behind a subscription paywall. The latest example is the removal of the exercise swap feature, similar to what happened in the February update (which was thankfully reversed at the time).

What’s especially disappointing is the lack of transparency—these changes aren’t mentioned in the update notes, which usually just say “bug fixes.” It feels like features are quietly being taken away without informing users, and that’s a frustrating shift from how things started.

At the end of the day, this app used to stand out for all the right reasons—it offered something genuinely different from the typical fitness app. Now, it’s hard to tell it apart from the rest. It’s disappointing to see how far it’s drifted from what made it special.

title: Great
body: Great programs. Needs Apple Watch integration

title: App keeps unexpectedly closing
body: Love the app but as of late, the app will randomly close and then I lose all my progress for the workout. EXTREMELY frustrating I want to throw my phone across the gym

title: Love the app but there are bugs
body: I love how I can write my own workouts and keep track of my weight/reps. I’ve tried using notebooks but always forget them at home. I always have my phone so this was a game changer for me. It helps me be more consistent with what I’m lifting. There are bugs though. One week it only copied 2 exercises from each day and this morning it extended my 8 week workout program to 12! I’m interested in the Pro version but I’m hesitant because of the bugs.

title: 2 Years In
body: Refreshing amount of programs.  Dedicated staff.  Constant updates based on user feedback.  Variety for pretty much every fitness goal.  This app is worth every penny for your health and future.  I’ve probably reviewed 5 apps in 20 years.   This is top notch.

title: Last update ruined it
body: Sadly this was my favorite workout app but the recent updates have basically made Pro a requirement. Probably going back to Hevy

title: Best workout plan ever
body: Very easy and friendly app

title: Boostcamp
body: The app is filled with plenty of workout programs. It is detailed and user friendly. I am doing the Hybrid Athletic Training Program and so far I am loving it. It is exactly what I need to maintain standards and it is tailored to my fitness goals. I recommend it specially if you are looking for a variety of workout routines and different challenges. Many of the features I like about this application are the timer and the plates calculator. Also, it gives the option to change a specific exercise if the equipment is not available.

title: Overwhelmingly satisfied!
body: This app soundly wallops its competition - and I’m not even a pro user! The free tier has everything you need to begin or maintain a fitness habit. Love the links to proper form accessible during a workout, and love that the app is so privacy-focused! I completely ditched JEFIT after trying this for a week and I’ve been so happy with it ever since. Great work team!

title: Great app
body:
Even if you’re new to the gym, they have 
 little video so you don’t have to go on YouTube all the time and it’s keeping me consistent

title: Bug with date entry
body: Really enjoying the app so far. Keep having this issue when entering dates on my workout plan. Keep putting in Jan. 31st and it keeps changing to Feb. 1st. Previous update has not fixed this issue. Minor but a bit annoying

title: Best free workout app
body: No reason to download another.

title: Solid app
body: Nice app. I use the free version, I’d definitely pay for Pro if there was Apple Watch integration.

title: Great but missing some basic exercise exercises
body: I really like this app and I think it’s the best tracking app out there for the most part but I don’t understand why there’s no cardio machines like a treadmill or stairstepper

title: Much promised – poor design – no support
body: I was interested in this app because it would allow me to create my own custom programs and attach video files so that I could remember proper technique. I spent creating a program and linking videos, but within days the video links were corrupted and inaccessible. I sent an email through the  support page, but I got no reply. The web UI is poor, and modifying or editing programs is clunky and unresponsive   While Boostcamp promises the ability to create your own workouts, it really wants to sell you the prepackaged templates that they have. I wish I had cancelled before an annual subscription kick in on day seven – definitely not worth $60 a year. Caveat emptor.

title: Latest update is a money grab.
body: I loved this workout app until the last update. They keep pushing towards making you buy the membership. The latest update doesn’t let you swap out exercises with your own alternative. Just a money grab at that point. Uninstalled and will replace with something else.

title: I love this app
body: I’ve had this app for over a year. I think it’s great. I’ve paid for it. I’ve used it free. It’s great. The ONLY issue I have is with the update that doesn’t allow you to edit your own alternative anymore for free. Which hinders my ability to edit the workouts. It’s fine. It’s a business decision. I still love the app.

title: Awesome fitness app
body:
This is the app that got me jacked!! 3 years ago I started weight lifting with the Reddit ppl program and had a great experience. 

Now I’m trying to get back into lifting as a form of regular exercise and the app is sleek and bug free. I can even look back at all the workouts from back when I started :)

I heavily recommend getting on and following a program on boost camp

title: Feature request
body: When I add a set to my workout, please keep that set for the next week instead of having to check my history to see which exercises had additional sets.

title: Great App! Must have for lifters of all levels!
Awesome App
body: I was using a spreadsheet to track my workouts prior. I got the premium version and absolutely love it. It couldn’t be easier to find legit program, tweak it for tor your gym, and to track your progress along your workout journey. I would highly recommend!

title: Amazing
body:
This app is amazing!!! It is exactly what I was looking for! I can import exercises and see what other programs are out there. Way easier than Google sheets (what I was using before).

Only thing I would change: ability to more easily add a week after creating a program. I have to start all over again if I miscount and it takes a lot of time

title: A usable app without paying?
body: Yes!! There is of course a pro option, but incredible content and usability for free. Exactly what I was looking for and so good it makes me WANT to pay for the pro version. Other developers take note, this is what we want!

title: Atrocious
body: First thing it tells you is go read Wendlers book for the first 3 sets of every exercise.

title: Great app
body: I’ve used a ton of “free” workout apps and this one is by far the best

title: Perfection
body:
I don’t want to name names but after using a fitness app for 3 years and see it go down, I tried to find a new app but couldn’t find one that had the tools, usability, flexibility, design, and programs that could meet my fitness needs. After trying a few apps found this and I tell ya this checks all those boxes! 

The app is designed perfectly, allows me to even create new custom workouts if it doesn’t exist in the database, and being able to get onto programs made by professionals is amazing! When it comes to seeing results, programs are very important, and this app connects you to pros who can get you the results you are looking for with their programs! 

And, all the data and graphics you get is best, but being able to share those graphs and workouts with others is so cool! 

I love this app and will recommend to everyone who is looking for amazing workout programs with amazing app with great capabilities!

title: Good
body:
I think the app is great for people who want their workouts already laid out for them. Plenty of different programs to choose from. Although I am a little upset they took out all the cardio programs. 

There is very little instruction for beginners on proper form. There is a little demonstration but just from that, If I didn’t heavy somebody with experience working with me my form would be bad and I wouldn’t know any better from using the app.

title: Literally does not work
body: I click the app to open and it’s just blank. 1 star

title: No Apple Watch support?
body:
The app itself is amazing however I’m giving 2 stars because of the lack of Apple Watch support, I get a notification timer but it lacks the ability to add inputs like weight selection and auto move to next set..
When (or if ) it comes soon I’ll definitely update my review to higher rating.

title: Solid app now bloated
body: Remember downloading this several years ago after one of the creators posted about it on Reddit. Funny enough they said it’d always be free with no catches. Sounds like a joke now. Every upgrade and especially the premium tier popups have made this app unbearable to use. Sometimes, less is more.

title: Great but wish there was an option for lifetime subscription
body: I think the app is phenomenal but I think it would be beneficial for there to be a lifetime subscription. I will never buy a monthly one but a more expensive forever one would interest me.

title: Great App but…..
body:
I honestly feel the timer between sets should be a free feature, please note you’ll have to track your own time between sets.

Also, it’s insanely hard to reorder exercises. The app doesn’t register your touch/input 9/10 times. If you create your own workouts, take care to order the exercises correctly. 

Other than that the app is great. Programs are pretty decent. Virtually every exercise is in the library.

title: Great if not so buggy
body:
Tons of frustrating bugs to deal
With. Rest timer only alerts intermittently and often just turns off; typing keyboard won’t show up and app has to be restarted; often after finishing and completing a workout, the timer keeps running and workout has to be opened, edited, and resaved. 

It’s a great concept of an app but the functionality is not up to par.

title: Designed by the best coaches in bodybuilding and fitness
body: I get access to programs by some of the best coaches in natural bodybuilding and fitness including Eric Helms, Alberto Nunez, Layne Norton, GVS, Natural Hypertrophy and more!

title: Great until pop ups
body: Loved the app before and was cool using the free mode and sometimes paid but the addition of having a pop up every time the app is closed is really annoying and greedy. When will devs learn that having a pop up trying to coerce me to pay will only make me hate the app more not feel more tempted to buy it. Maybe if you offered a pay once offer I would do it. At the end of the day this is a glorified database not some revolutionary app that constantly changes.

title: Slow and limited
body: The app is slow and buggy. The feature is very limited. If the non-stop in app advertising gets to you, the paid version actually lets you manage your work outs but at that rate a google doc is just a s good.

title: Modifying workouts doesn’t work properly
body:
Basic functionality of this app is pretty nice, even if it’s missing some programs I’d like it to have.

Biggest flaw with the app is that modifying programs doesn’t properly save. It’s a minor annoyance but for the relatively high cost of this app I’d expect such basic functionality to work properly.

title: Easy
body: This app makes it easy to keep track of your workouts. And I’m using boring but big 531 and it recommends great accessory exercises and is able to tell me exactly what weight I should be using

title: Relentless Spammers
body: I have unsubscribed three times from their spam.  They happily keep on sending it.  To violate such a basic contract is a real indicator of the philosophy and approach of this company.  Pretty disappointing.

title: Great workouts, too many ads
body: Brother the workouts you find on here are great. But oh my gosh every time I open up the app I get like 300 things to sign up for their yearly garbage to use the app. Like at this point I should just take screenshots of my workout cause it’s so annoying to open the app now.

title: Good but still buggy
body: Overall I like that app but for whatever reason it randomly won’t save my workouts.  I click finished, every looks good, and then the workout just disappears from my history.  Will consider upgrading to premium when that’s resolved.  It’s happened to 6 out of 30 workouts so far.

title: Has come a long way
body: I love this app, I do think there is some market for tiers of subscriptions instead of making it all or none for the premium stuff. I also wish I wasn’t spammed with the “upgrade to pro” page every time I open the app. Other than that it’s flawless and keep up the great work!
